note: Stretch 36:42-42:20 is Latin-transliterated by the engine. D10 (بندار) is him repeating a phrase she was teaching that moment (same teaching as agreed A33), so dropped. D3 dropped: حروف إنجليزي with an invariable language adjective is normal Levantine usage. A46 challenged: Amal's own C12 example is 3amalna tamreen kteer.

row.why: Clock time takes el- (3al-tmaanye); she let it pass and asked what he drank. Low because the engine may have swallowed an assimilated el-.

rulings.why: Answer to 'what time did you wake up'; clock time needs el- (E2). Unvoiced, low confidence because the engine can drop the assimilated el-.

row.medi_said: يفهم عربي، بس ما، آآآم، م-م-ما، ما يقدر أكتب عربي.
row.why: The subject is still Google Meet (يفهم عربي), so 'it can't write' needs يكتب, not أكتب (I write); she let it pass.
row.english: It understands Arabic but it can't write Arabic.

rulings.why: Subject is Google Meet throughout (Amal had just fixed تفهم -> يفهم at 14:08); أكتب is first person. Separate wrong piece from A11 (ما يقدر).
Not an error: حروف إنجليزي (language word used as invariable adjective, like حكي عربي) is normal spoken Levantine; Amal said مم-هم.

row.medi_said: شو، شو أكتر بقدر، شو أكتر بقدر أعمل؟
row.amal_said: ولا إشي. خلاص، زي ما بدك.
row.why: After she said his answer was too short he asked 'what more can I do'; 'what else' is شو كمان, أكتر is the comparative - an English calque she answered without fixing.

rulings.why: Calque of 'what more'; she let it pass. Unscored vocab-B, low confidence.

row.medi_said: إحنا، إحنا بنخ-- بنخط. Ben-- it's just بنخط، right?
row.why: The verb is خطط; he cut it to بنخط and checked it, she recast بنخطط and he repeated it at 43:42.

rulings.why: He produced the wrong form and she recast it; he repeated her بنخطط. Not a self-fix.

row.medi_said: على كلٍ. على كلٍ شو، اه، شو، اه، بعصب، بعصب. I'm asking you.
row.amal_said: اه. بس، اه، let's not use it I think. بلاش. Sounds wrong. ... But if you want to say, you would say بشكل عام.
row.why: He asked how to say 'in general' (45:14 'do you say الكل if I wanna say in general?'), she first allowed على كل, then on hearing it said it sounds wrong and supplied بشكل عام - a didn't-know, not a slip.
row.english: In general, what makes me angry...

rulings.why: Tier 0 asked: the whole exchange is him asking how to say 'in general' and Amal herself first said على كل could work; she then supplied بشكل عام.

row.medi_said: لما أنا لما أزآن. ... أز، أزأل.
row.why: Her question used زهآن; he mangled it into أزآن / أزأل, she said No twice and gave زهآن, which he repeated at 55:28.

rulings.why: Explicit No twice plus her form; أزأل is not just a dropped letter. The later لما بزهأ -> لما أزهأ is agreed A42 (grammar), a different piece.

row.medi_said: So it has to be, has to be، اه، issue can، اه، can issue- ... So if I wanna say it has to be something really bad.
row.amal_said: ما في can. It's it. ... لازم يكون issue، issue سيء.
row.why: He asked how to say 'it has to be something really bad' and she supplied لازم يكون; he repeated it at 48:28.
row.english: It has to be something really bad.

rulings.why: Didn't-know: he asked in English and she supplied لازم يكون. Tier 0.

row.medi_said: ما زبت. زبت is... It means it's okay, right? It's positive.
row.amal_said: ما زبت. It-- معنى it didn't work out.
row.right: ما زبت = it didn't work out
row.why: She asked what ما زبت means; he guessed the opposite (positive) and she gave 'it didn't work out', which he accepted ('That's right').

rulings.why: Real listening miss (wrong meaning guessed, like agreed A16), mode listening.

Duplicate of agreed A33: he is imitating ‹Bindir›, a phrase Amal had introduced seconds earlier (36:51) for 'take care of'; a vowel slip while repeating a just-taught word is part of that teaching, and the engine vowel may be S4.

row.medi_said: ooh, I wanna say both of us. Do I just say ‹tinen›? Or-
row.why: He asked how to say 'both of us'; Amal supplied ahna il tinen and he used it at 39:07.

rulings.why: Didn't-know he asked about; she supplied the phrase. Tier 0.

row.medi_said: ‹Ana lazim, astamel il fa'il›, instead, instead is... Oh my God.
row.amal_said: Oh, we don't know instead. No, no. Don't worry. ‹Badal›.
row.why: He could not say 'instead' and stalled; Amal supplied badal (noting it was not taught yet).
row.english: I should use the verb instead.

challenges.why: عملنا تمرين كتير is the exact example in bucket C12 (3amalna tamreen kteer); تمرين as a collective after عملنا is fine, and Amal's عنجد؟ reacts to the content, not the form. Likely not an error.
